citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
During this focused inspection, it was found that the facility has not completed a written Program of Veterinary Care for
animals in the facility.
A written Program of Veterinary Care is required for all USDA licensed facilities.
A written Program of Veterinary Care is needed to ensure that all regulated animals in a facility receive appropriate and
timely preventative medical care and treatment, as deterimined by a licensed veterinarian.
Correct by 08-15-2026

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
A focused inspection was conducted by a USDA VMO on 04AUG2026 to verify veterinary evaluation and treatment of a
young Quaker/Monk Parrot previously listed under an AWA 2.40(b)(3) non-compliance citation on 24JULY2026. The
correction date given on the report was 01AUGUST2026.
The young Quaker/Monk Parrot cited on the July 24, 2026 USDA report had not yet been evaluated by a veterinarian at
the time of the USDA focused inspection on August 04, 2026. The young parrot appeared alert and in good body
condition, however, was also observed to be splay-legged and unable to stand or ambulate normally during inspection.
Direct and timely communication with a licensed veterinarian is required when problems arise affecting animal health,
well-being or behavior. Failure to communicate animal health issues in a timely manner to your veterinarian may result in
further animal injury and distress.
The facility owner agreed to take the bird to a nearby veterinary clinic accompanied by the USDA inspector during the
inspection visit. The parrot was taken by a facility employee to a nearby veterinary clinic where it was evaluated and left
for follow up treatment with the clinic veterinarian.
The inspection was conducted on August 04, 2026 and the exit interview was conducted on August 07, 2026 with facility
representatives.
